desc:
An undirected tree has n nodes numbered 0..n-1 and n - 1 edges [a, b]. The distance between two nodes is the number of edges on the path between them.

Return an array answer of length n where answer[v] is the sum of the distances from node v to all the other nodes.

n = 5, edges = [[0,1],[1,2],[1,3],[3,4]]

answer[0] = 1+2+2+3 = 8      answer[1] = 1+1+1+2 = 5
answer = [8, 5, 8, 6, 9]
constraints: edges.length = n - 1 and the edges form a tree
Running a BFS from every node (O(n<sup>2</sup>)) is too slow; an O(n) method exists
hints: Computing the answer for one fixed root is easy: add up the depths of all nodes. The hard part is doing it for every root.
Compare the answer of a node p with the answer of its child c. Moving the root from p to c brings the nodes in c's subtree one step closer and sends all other nodes one step farther.
Root at 0, compute size[v] and answer[0], then for each child c of p use answer[c] = answer[p] - size[c] + (n - size[c]), processing nodes in BFS order.
editorial: This is the classic rerooting technique: compute the answer for one root, then derive the answer for each neighbour in O(1).

Root the tree at 0 and get a BFS order with parents. Compute size[v] (subtree sizes) by sweeping the order backwards, and compute answer[0] as the sum of all depths. Now take a node p and its child c. If the root moves from p to c, then every node inside c's subtree (there are size[c] of them) gets one edge closer, and every other node (n - size[c] of them) gets one edge farther. So answer[c] = answer[p] - size[c] + (n - size[c]). Sweep the BFS order forwards and fill every answer.
Total time O(n) and space O(n). The largest possible value is the sum on a path, n(n-1)/2, which is under 4.5 · 10<sup>8</sup> for the allowed n, so it fits in 32 bits.
